proposals.before: Outside the gate, civil officials stood in the eastern hall; the Duke of Jie and Duke of Xi before the western hall; military officials south of the Duke of Jie, slightly back, each grade in its own row;
proposals.after: Outside the gate, civil officials stood in the eastern hall; the Duke of Jie and the Duke of Xi before the western hall; military officials south of the Duke of Jie, slightly back, each grade in its own row;
proposals.reason: The second duke title drops the parallel article present in Chinese 介公、酅公 and in this unit's literal English.

proposals.before: The Imperial Household Service placed seats for hall ascent: third-rank civil officials and above southeast of the throne, facing west;
proposals.after: The Imperial Household Service placed seats for hall ascent: third-rank civil officials and above again southeast of the throne, facing west;
proposals.reason: Chinese 又 marks a repeated seating placement southeast of the throne; the idiomatic English drops that adverb, unlike the literal rendering.

proposals.before: The Director of the Imperial Household Bureau advanced to the steps, knelt, and said: "Your servant So-and-so requests leave to offer longevity wine to the ministers."
proposals.after: The Chamberlain for Ceremonials advanced to the steps, knelt, and said: "Your servant So-and-so requests leave to offer longevity wine to the ministers."
proposals.reason: 光祿卿 is the Chamberlain for Ceremonials (Court of Imperial Entertainments), not the Imperial Household Bureau, which would suggest 殿中 or 尚舍 offices.

proposals.before: The Director of the Imperial Household Bureau advanced to the foot of the steps, knelt, and memorialized: "Your servant So-and-so says: Request permission to offer longevity wine to the ministers."
proposals.after: The Chamberlain for Ceremonials advanced to the foot of the steps, knelt, and memorialized: "Your servant So-and-so says: Request permission to offer longevity wine to the ministers."
proposals.reason: Same office mistranslation of 光祿卿 as Imperial Household Bureau in the literal English.

proposals.before: The emperor rose; the imperial carriage returned through the east chamber; east- and west-facing groups left in sequence.
proposals.after: The emperor rose; the imperial carriage entered from the east chamber; east- and west-facing groups left in sequence.
proposals.reason: Chinese 入自東房 means the carriage entered from the east chamber, not that it returned through it.

proposals.before: Enthronement at the Hall to Invest the Crown Prince
proposals.after: Holding court at the hall to invest the crown prince
proposals.reason: 臨軒冊 is court-front investiture by patent, not enthronement.

proposals.before: Enthronement at the hall to invest the crown prince.
proposals.after: The crown prince is invested at the hall front.
proposals.reason: 冊皇太子 is investiture by patent; 臨軒 is holding court, not enthronement.

proposals.before: In early spring the Rites Minister read the ordinances for three days, then memorialized the monthly ordinances for public proclamation.
proposals.after: In early spring, three days before the ordinances were read, the Minister of Rites memorialized that the monthly ordinances be read, and they were then proclaimed.
proposals.reason: 先讀令三日 is three days before the reading, not a three-day recitation by the minister.

proposals.before: In the first month of spring the Minister of Rites first read the ordinances for three days and memorialized the reading of the monthly ordinances, which were proclaimed accordingly.
proposals.after: In the first month of spring, three days before the ordinances were read, the Minister of Rites memorialized the reading of the monthly ordinances, which were then proclaimed.
proposals.reason: 先讀令三日 marks the memorial three days before the reading, not that the minister himself read for three days.

proposals.before: All in double rows, precedence west and north.
proposals.after: All in double rows, with precedence to the west.
proposals.reason: Chinese 西上 marks west as the place of honor only; the English invents a northern precedence that the source does not state.

proposals.before: All in double rows with precedence to the west and north.
proposals.after: All in double rows with precedence to the west.
proposals.reason: Chinese 西上 is west-as-superior only; adding north is not in the source.

proposals.before: the chief musician stood northeast of the bells, facing south.
proposals.after: another station was northeast of the bell-chimes, facing south.
proposals.reason: 其一位 continues 舉麾位: a second banner station, not a chief musician. The English invents a person the Chinese does not name.

proposals.before: the chief musician stood northeast of the bell frame, facing south.
proposals.after: its other position was northeast of the bell-chimes, facing south.
proposals.reason: 其一位 is the second 舉麾位, not a musician; the literal English invents a named office-holder.

proposals.before: All in double rows, precedence west and north.
proposals.after: All in double rows, with precedence to the west.
proposals.reason: Chinese 西上 again marks only western precedence; north is an invention.

proposals.before: All in double rows with precedence to the west and north.
proposals.after: All in double rows with precedence to the west.
proposals.reason: Chinese 西上 does not include northern precedence.

proposals.before: The Director of Ritual Observances set outside stations before each waiting area, each grade in separate facing rows, precedence west and north.
proposals.after: The Director of Ritual Observances set outside stations before each waiting area, each grade in separate facing rows, with precedence to the west.
proposals.reason: 西上 is western precedence only; the English adds north without support.

proposals.before: The Director of Ritual Observances set outside positions before each waiting station, each grade in separate rows facing one another, precedence to the west and north.
proposals.after: The Director of Ritual Observances set outside positions before each waiting station, each grade in separate rows facing one another, with precedence to the west.
proposals.reason: 西上 does not authorize northern precedence in the literal English.

proposals.before: Offices first nominated retired grand tutors and preceptors; the most virtuous and eldest became Three Elder and Five Senior; fifth-rank retirees were State Elders, sixth rank and below Common Elders.
proposals.after: The offices first nominated retired members of the Three Tutors and Three Dukes; the one of highest virtue and age was made Three Elder, and the next was made Five Senior; retired officials of the fifth rank and above were State Elders, and those of the sixth rank and below were Common Elders.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic English fuses two separately appointed men (一人為三老，次一人為五更) into one, and renders 三公 as preceptors rather than the Three Dukes.

proposals.before: As the procession approached, advance officials took outside stations; students in blue collars entered to place.
proposals.after: As the procession approached, advance officials took outside stations; students in blue collars entered to their places.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic English is ungrammatical: 入就位 means the students entered and took their stations, not “entered to place.”

proposals.before: the Ritual Director brought other elders out to stand behind them;
proposals.after: the Ritual Director brought other elders out to stand behind the Three Elder and Five Senior;
proposals.reason: The Chinese names 三老、五更 as the people stood behind; the idiomatic English collapses them to a pronoun and loses the referents.

proposals.before: They stood west of the gate, facing east; the Ritual Director led other elders in behind.
proposals.after: The Three Elder and Five Senior stood west of the gate, facing east with precedence north; the Ritual Director led other elders in behind.
proposals.reason: The sentence subject is 三老、五更 and the orientation is 東面北上; the idiomatic English uses an unclear “They” and omits northern precedence.

proposals.before: Announcers set relish before the host; he ascended from the east, announcers set divided meat; he knelt, goblet left, offered meat, dipped relish, offered between baskets and beans, offered and tasted wine, rose, descended south, returned to the host steps, knelt north, drained the goblet, set it at the east end, took a cup from the basket for the return toast, knelt north, set the cup, bowed, and rose with cup.
proposals.after: Announcers set dried meat and relish before the host; he ascended from the east, announcers set divided meat; he knelt, goblet left, offered meat, dipped relish, offered between baskets and beans, offered and tasted wine, rose, descended south, returned to the host steps, knelt north, drained the goblet, set it at the east end, took a cup from the basket for the return toast, knelt north, set the cup, bowed, and rose with cup.
proposals.reason: Chinese 薦脯、醢 names both dried meat and relish before the host's mat; the idiomatic line drops 脯.

proposals.before: Announcers presented dried meat and relish before the host's mat; the host ascended the mat from the east by the north, announcers set the divided offering; the host knelt, held the goblet left, offered dried meat right, dipped in relish, offered between baskets and beans, offered and tasted wine, rose, descended south of the mat, again stood on the host steps, knelt northward, finished the goblet, held the goblet and rose, knelt and set the goblet at the east end of the sequence, rose, went to the basket, knelt and took a cup to fill for the return toast, again stood on the host steps, knelt northward, set the cup, then bowed and held the cup and rose.
proposals.after: Announcers presented dried meat and relish before the host's mat; the host ascended the mat from the east by the north, announcers set the divided offering; the host knelt, held the goblet left, offered dried meat right, dipped in relish, offered between baskets and beans, offered and tasted wine, rose, descended south of the mat, again stood on the host steps, knelt northward, finished the goblet, held the goblet and rose, knelt and set the goblet at the east end of the east side-wall, rose, went to the basket, knelt and took a cup to fill for the return toast, again stood on the host steps, knelt northward, set the cup, then bowed and held the cup and rose.
proposals.reason: 東序端 is the east end of the hall's east side-wall (序), not a 'sequence'.

proposals.before: The host went to the east end of the sequence, knelt, took a goblet, rose, and went to the vessel to fill it.
proposals.after: The host went to the east end of the east side-wall, knelt, took a goblet, rose, and went to the vessel to fill it.
proposals.reason: 東序端 is the east end of the hall's east side-wall (序), not a 'sequence'.

proposals.before: Announcers set relish before the Assistant; he advanced from the north, ascended, offered meat and relish, libated, rose, descended south, knelt north, drained the goblet, handed it to the host; the host refilled and toasted on the west steps, stood east of the Assistant, knelt north, set the goblet, bowed, and rose.
proposals.after: Announcers set dried meat and relish before the Assistant; he advanced from the north, ascended, offered meat and relish, libated, rose, descended south, knelt north, drained the goblet, handed it to the host; the host refilled and toasted on the west steps, stood east of the Assistant, knelt north, set the goblet, bowed, and rose.
proposals.reason: Chinese 薦脯、醢 names both dried meat and relish; the idiomatic line drops 脯.

proposals.before: The recipient left the mat, came from the west, and stood north of the Assistant facing north.
proposals.after: The recipient left the mat, came from the west, and stood to the right of the Assistant facing north.
proposals.reason: Chinese 立於介右 means standing at the Assistant's right, not north of the Assistant; 北面 is orientation only.

proposals.before: The recipient of the toast left the mat, advanced from the west, and stood north of the Assistant facing north.
proposals.after: The recipient of the toast left the mat, advanced from the west, and stood to the right of the Assistant facing north.
proposals.reason: Chinese 立於介右 is position at the Assistant's right; both English fields wrongly render 右 as north.

proposals.before: The Director of Corrections went to the host steps, faced east, and requested orders from the host; the host said: "Request that my lord sit with the Guest."
proposals.after: The Director of Corrections went to the host steps, faced east, and requested orders from the host; the host said: "Request sitting with the Guest."
proposals.reason: 請坐於賓 has no honorific equivalent to "my lord"; that addressee is invented in the literal English.

decisions.reason: 介公、酅公 are already named as the Duke of Jie and Duke of Xi; inserting a second definite article is only a stylistic parallel and does not correct an error of meaning.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 介公、酅公在西朝堂之前

decisions.reason: The seating is correctly given as third-rank civil officials and above southeast of the throne, facing west; omitting 又 does not change that placement, and inserting “again” is a discourse polish rather than a required factual repair.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 文官三品以上又御座東南，西向

decisions.after: The Chief Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments advanced to the steps, knelt, and said: "Your servant So-and-so requests leave to offer longevity wine to the ministers."
decisions.reason: 光祿卿 heads 光祿寺, the Court of Imperial Entertainments, so “Imperial Household Bureau” is wrong; the proposed “Chamberlain for Ceremonials” names 太常卿 instead and must be replaced with the Tang office title.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 光祿卿進詣階間，跪奏稱

decisions.after: The Chief Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments advanced to the foot of the steps, knelt, and memorialized: "Your servant So-and-so says: Request permission to offer longevity wine to the ministers."
decisions.reason: The same 光祿卿 is misrendered as Imperial Household Bureau; “Chamberlain for Ceremonials” is the wrong court, so the literal line should name the Chief Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 光祿卿進詣階間，跪奏稱

decisions.reason: 入自東房 means the imperial carriage entered from the east chamber; “returned through” reverses the path.
臨軒冊皇太子 is holding court at the hall front to invest the crown prince by patent, not an enthronement.
The same heading with a period is investiture at the hall front, not enthronement; the proposed literal matches 冊皇太子 and 臨軒.
先讀令三日 is three days before the reading, confirmed by the following 前三日 preparations; the original wrongly has the minister reciting for three days.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 禮部尚書先讀令三日奏讀月令，承以宣告

decisions.reason: The literal likewise misreads 先讀令三日 as a three-day recitation; the minister memorializes the monthly-ordinance reading three days in advance.
俱重行西上 marks only west as superior; “north” is not in the Chinese.
The literal “west and north” likewise adds a northern precedence absent from 西上.
其一位 continues the 舉麾位 of the previous sentence: a second banner station northeast of the bell rack, not a chief musician.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 其一位於樂縣東北，南向

decisions.reason: The literal invents the same office-holder; 其一位 is the other banner-raising position, facing south.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 其一位於樂縣東北，南向

decisions.reason: 皆重行西上 again gives western precedence only; northern honor is invented.
The matching literal interpolation of north is unsupported by 西上.
門外位…西上 likewise ranks west as superior only; the added northern precedence is not in the source.
The literal “west and north” repeats the same unsupported northern ranking on 西上.
The source names retired 三師、三公 and then two men, 一人為三老 and 次一人為五更; the original fuses the honorees and misrenders 三公 as preceptors.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 三師、三公致仕者，用其德行及年高者一人為三老，次一人為五更

decisions.reason: 入就位 is entering and taking stations; “entered to place” is ungrammatical and incomplete.
立於三老、五更之後 is already clear from the preceding sentence naming those two; “behind them” is accurate and the spelled-out names are only a stylistic expansion.
東面北上 requires facing east with north as the place of honor; the original drops 北上.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 三老、五更於門西，東面北上

decisions.reason: 薦脯、醢 places both dried meat and relish before the host; the idiomatic line omits 脯.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 贊者薦脯、醢于主人席前

decisions.reason: 東序端 is the end of the eastern side-wall, not a “sequence.”
詣東序端 is likewise the eastern side-wall end; “sequence” is a mistranslation of 序.
薦脯、醢 before the Assistant’s mat again names dried meat and relish; dropping 脯 omits half the offering.
北面立於介右 is facing north while standing at the Assistant’s right; “north of the Assistant” confuses orientation with position.
The literal makes the same 右/north error; the recipient stands to the Assistant’s right, facing north.
請坐於賓 requests sitting with the Guest; “my lord” is an invented addressee not in the host’s words.
